name: RAM size
plain: Reads total memory in bytes with no prompt.
meaning: Maps almost directly to device price tier (2 to 16 GB) and is a stable fingerprint bit. Apps use it to size caches.

android.note: Exact total bytes; app heap class 128 to 512 MB

ios.api_surface: Exact bytes; iPhones range about 1 to 12 GB

limits.headline: Can see how much memory your phone has, down to the exact byte, with no prompt
limits.user_action: Nothing. The app checks when it starts to choose how heavy to run
can: See total memory in bytes on Android and iPhone
See the app's Android memory class, about 128 to 512 MB
Check if your Android phone is a low memory device
cannot: Use more memory than the system allows for the app
See what other apps are using
Tell who you are from the memory size alone
limits.differs: Android also shows a memory class and a low memory flag. iPhones range from about 1 to 12 GB.

story.what_it_is: An app can see how much memory your phone has.
story.for_you: You never see it. It hints at how fast and costly your phone is. Apps use it to decide how much to keep ready in memory.
story.for_makers: Makers size their caches and pick quality settings from it. It maps closely to device price and is a stable fingerprint detail.

use_cases.example: A big game loads high detail textures on a 12 GB phone and small ones on a 3 GB phone.
A video editor limits clip length on low memory phones so it does not crash.
A feed app keeps fewer videos ready in memory on small phones.
An AR app picks a lighter 3D model on phones with little memory.
A store app guesses your phone's price tier to decide which ads to show.
An ad firm adds memory size to a fingerprint.

risks: Hints at what you can afford

story.ios_note: Reads total memory with no prompt.

technical_bounds: Static per device model, so low entropy within a model
